text: Good API design is crucial for creating software that is easy to use and maintain. Most modern services use REST APIs, which rely on standard HTTP methods like GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE to interact with resources. When designing these systems, it is essential to use clear and consistent endpoints, such as `/users` or `/orders`, rather than confusing actions in the URL. Every request should return an appropriate status code, like `200` for success or `404` for a missing resource, so developers can quickly understand what happened. Furthermore, thorough documentation is vital; it guides developers on how to use the API correctly. Finally, always plan for versioning, such as `/v1/`, to make changes without breaking existing users. These practices ensure a stable and friendly experience for everyone.
